extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and members of the public requesting patent application records
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing confidentiality, public inspection, status information, petitions for access, and procedures for obtaining copies of U.S. patent application files (including IFW and published/unpublished cases) under 37 CFR §§1.11, 1.14 and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status information of an application (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information of an application means only the following information: (A) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (B) whether the application has been published; (C) the application number or the serial number plus any one of the filing date of the national application, the international filing date or the date of entry into the national stage; and (D) whether another application claims the benefit of the application and, if so, the numerical identifier of the application, the specified relationship between the applications (e.g., continuation), whether the application is pending, abandoned or patented, and whether the application has been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff and public requests for status information should be limited to these items. Requesters seeking status should check PAIR; FIU can provide status when appropriate (see MPEP §1730).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is entitled to status information (authorized requesters)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester is entitled to status information if the requester is: (A) an inventor; (B) an attorney or agent of record in the application; (C) an assignee of record in the application; or (D) a person with written authority from (A), (B), or (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester is one of these, they are entitled to status information. If asking about whether a reply was received or when an Office action can be expected, direct the requester to call the Technology Center (TC) assigned to the application. TC assignment can be determined from PALM Intranet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public requester entitlement when application is identified in published patent document
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is not an authorized party but the application is (1) identified by application number (or serial number and filing date) in a published patent document, or (2) an application claiming the benefit of the filing date of an application identified by application number (or serial number and filing date) in a published patent document, then a written request including a copy of the published patent document which refers to the specific application must be provided when requesting status information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the published patent document is not in English, a translation of the pertinent part must be included. The published patent document may be presented in person to the FIU or by written correspondence (e.g., facsimile). Written correspondence must include a return address or facsimile number. PALM Intranet should be used to determine status and continuity data; limited status information for related child applications may be provided as per 37 CFR 1.14(a)(2)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on continuity/chain information provided to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Other information contained on continuity/chain screens (e.g., whether the application is a CIP, continuation or divisional, the date of abandonment, and the issue date) may be confidential and should not be communicated to non-authorized requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule about extent of chain: the rule applies only to subsequent and not prior applications. Only the limited status data enumerated in the 'status information' definition may be given to the public absent authorization or other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PALM and IFW notes for office personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining current location or status of an application, Office personnel should use PALM. If the application is an Image File Wrapper (IFW) application, no physical location is associated with the file; consult the IFW Manual for the location of any artifact files. For pre-07 series applications not in PALM, contact the FIU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PALM Intranet should be used to determine status, child applications, and continuity data. If IFW/Internet access is not yet available for IFW applications, the file itself will not be available to the public for inspection, though copies may be obtainable per 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii) and (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Files open to the public (37 CFR 1.11) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, drawings, and all papers relating to the file of an abandoned published application, a patent, or a statutory invention registration are open to inspection by the public, and copies may be obtained upon payment of the fee set forth in §1.19(b)(2). Reissue applications and other papers where the Office has accepted a request to open the complete application to inspection are open to inspection and copies furnished upon paying the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements in the Official Gazette for reissue and reexamination include prescribed bibliographic items (filing date, numbers, title, class/subclass, inventor, owner of record, attorney/agent, examining group). Reexamination and Director-initiated reexamination announcements and many reexamination/reexamination-file papers are open per 37 CFR 1.11 and 1.14 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of patent application information (37 CFR 1.14) — overarching principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning the filing, pendency, or subject matter of an application, including status information and access to the application, will only be given to the public as set forth in §1.11 or §1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All access and disclosure determinations must be made in light of these statutory/regulatory confidentiality rules and the enumerated exceptions in §1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: patented applications and statutory invention registrations (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of an application that has issued as a patent or published as a statutory invention registration is available to the public as set forth in §1.11(a). A copy of the patent application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document in the file may be provided upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 37 CFR 1.11/1.19 fee rules and Certification Division/ FIU procedures to obtain copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: published abandoned applications (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of an abandoned application that has been published as a patent application publication is available to the public and a copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document may be provided to any person upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a redacted copy was used for publication, the copy provided may be limited to the redacted version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: published pending applications (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document in the file of a pending application that has been published may be provided to any person upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)). If a redacted copy was used for publication, the copy may be limited to the redacted copy. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application that has been published, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (h) of §1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must follow fee/payment rules. Paper file access to pending apps is generally prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: unpublished abandoned applications identified or relied upon (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file contents of an unpublished, abandoned application may be made available to the public if the application is identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, a U.S. patent application publication, or an international patent application publication published in accordance with PCT Article 21(2). An application is considered identified when the application number or serial number and filing date, first named inventor, title and filing date or other application-specific information are provided in the text of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file contents may also be made available if benefit of the abandoned application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365 in an application that has issued as a U.S. patent or published. A written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the file contents of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)), if the benefit of the application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365 in an application that has issued as a U.S. patent, published as a statutory invention registration, or published as a patent application publication (or international publication per PCT Article 21(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (h) of §1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: unpublished pending applications incorporated by reference or otherwise identified (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application as originally filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§1.19(b)), if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, or international patent application publication published per PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (h) of §1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a petition for access or a power to inspect is required (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that were not published or patented, that are not subject of a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365 in an application that has issued or published, or are not identified in a published document, are not available to the public. If an application is identified only in the file contents of another application but not in the published patent or application itself, a granted petition for access or a power to inspect is necessary to obtain the application or a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition process (see paragraph (h)) applies; otherwise access is denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for access — requirements and process (37 CFR 1.14(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition by a member of the public seeking access to, or copies of, all or part of any pending or abandoned application preserved in confidence must include: (1) the fee set forth in §1.17(h); and (2) a showing that access is necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or that special circumstances exist which warrant petitioner being granted access to all or part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should include post office address (with ZIP), telephone and facsimile numbers. Petitions are handled in the Office of Patent Legal Administration unless the application is involved in an interference. Petition may be filed with proof of service on applicant or in duplicate (duplicate will be sent by Office to applicant). A separate petition with fee must be filed for each application. Each petition should state why access is desired and why petitioner believes entitled. Applicant normally is given a limited period (e.g., ~3 weeks) to state objection. If applicant has no objection, petition will be granted; if objection or no response, decide on record. If access granted, applicant's objections will be available to petitioner; if denied, petitioner won't receive copies of applicant objections. Determination hinges on whether 'special circumstances' under 35 U.S.C. 122 exist; examples include interference with competitor's business or attorney power-of-attorney issues. Alternative faster means may exist (e.g., obtaining power to inspect from assignee or inventor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All new applications filed on or after June 30, 2003 are stored as an Image File Wrapper (IFW), and the IFW is the official record of the application. There is no corresponding paper file wrapper for IFW applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When access to IFW applications is available to the public in the FIU and/or over the Internet, the public will be able to access pending and abandoned published patent applications pursuant to 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii) and (iii). If FIU/Internet access is not yet available for IFW applications, the file itself will not be available to the public for inspection, but copies of the application file may be obtained pursuant to 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii) and (iii). See IFW Manual for artifact file locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access where only part of an application is incorporated by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If only part of an application is incorporated by reference in a U.S. patent application publication or U.S. patent (e.g., 'the disclosure of a valve on page 5, lines 5-35, of application No. XX/YYY,YYY, is hereby incorporated by reference'), a petition for access is required to obtain access to or a copy of the incorporated material. Incorporation by reference of part of an application constitutes special circumstances warranting access to that part upon petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference is interpreted as a waiver of confidentiality of only that part of the original disclosure as filed, not the entire file. If applicant objects to access to the entire file, applicant must file two copies of the information incorporated by reference along with the objection; failure to provide the material within the time period will result in the entire application content (including prosecution history) being made available to the petitioner. The Office will not attempt to separate the noted materials from the remainder of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering copies from Certification Division / FIU (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of a patent application-as-filed and the contents of a patent application file wrapper may be ordered from the Certification Division with a facsimile request and payment of the appropriate fee under 37 CFR 1.19(b) by USPTO Deposit Account, or major credit cards, by any person having a right to access to the originally filed application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access. The Office does not provide for access to non-United States applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned applications meeting 1.14(a)(1)(iv) and FWC availability via FIU
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandoned applications meeting the requirements of 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv) (i.e., identified or relied upon) and any application open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11 may be obtained by any person upon written request to the FIU without the specific written authority of the applicant, assignee, attorney or agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abandoned non-IFW application identified in a U.S. patent application publication, U.S. patent or a U.S. application that is open to public inspection may be ordered for inspection through the FIU. If the abandoned application is contained within a pending File Wrapper Continuation (FWC) application, the requester will generally be directed to the appropriate Technology Center to inquire as to availability; if available it will be forwarded to FIU for requester pick-up. Abandoned file received by public must be returned to the FIU charge counter before the end of the same day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of chain of applications for which status information is available
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule on providing status/continuity information applies only to subsequent and not prior applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When providing status information about related applications, staff should limit disclosure to subsequent child applications as authorized and refrain from disclosing earlier/prior application details that are confidential.
